verses.original: Καὶ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν
verses.transliteration: Kai embas eis ploion dieperasen kai ēlthen eis tēn idian polin
verses.literal: Jesus got into . . . a boat crossed over and came to His own town
verses.literalPt: E, ENTRANDO no barco, passou para o outro lado, e chegou à sua cidade. E eis que lhe trouxeram um paralítico, deitado numa cama.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ Θάρσει τέκνον ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι
verses.transliteration: Kai idou prosepheron autō paralytikon epi klinēs beblēmenon kai idōn ho Iēsous tēn pistin autōn eipen tō paralytikō Tharsei teknon aphientai sou hai hamartiai
verses.literal: Just then . . . some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat When Jesus saw their faith He said to the paralytic Take courage son your sins are forgiven
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, vendo a fé deles, disse ao paralítico: Filho, tem bom ânimo, perdoados te são os teus pecados.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ
verses.transliteration: Kai idou tines tōn grammateōn eipan en heautois Houtos blasphēmei
verses.literal: On seeing this . . . some of the scribes said to themselves This man is blaspheming
verses.literalPt: E eis que alguns dos escribas diziam entre si: Ele blasfema.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἵνα‿ τί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai eidōs ho Iēsous tas enthymēseis autōn eipen Hina ti enthymeisthe ponēra en tais kardiais hymōn
verses.literal: But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said Why . . . do you harbor evil in your hearts
verses.literalPt: Mas Jesus, conhecendo os seus pensamentos, disse: Por que pensais mal em vossos corações?

verses.original: τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον εἰπεῖν Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει
verses.transliteration: ti gar estin eukopōteron eipein Aphientai sou hai hamartiai ē eipein Egeire kai peripatei
verses.literal: Which is easier to say Your sins are forgiven or to say Get up and walk
verses.literalPt: Pois, qual é mais fácil? dizer: Perdoados te são os teus pecados; ou dizer: Levanta-te e anda?

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου
verses.transliteration: hina de eidēte hoti exousian echei ho Huios tou anthrōpou epi tēs gēs aphienai hamartias tote legei tō paralytikō Egertheis aron sou tēn klinēn kai hypage eis ton oikon sou
verses.literal: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins Then He said to the paralytic Get up pick up your mat and go home
verses.literalPt: Ora, para que saibais que o Filho do homem tem na terra autoridade para perdoar pecados (disse então ao paralítico): Levanta-te, toma a tua cama, e vai para tua casa.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai egertheis apēlthen eis ton oikon autou
verses.literal: And the man got up and went home
verses.literalPt: E, levantando-se, foi para sua casa.

verses.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν Θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις
verses.transliteration: Idontes de hoi ochloi ephobēthēsan kai edoxasan ton Theon ton donta exousian toiautēn tois anthrōpois
verses.literal: When the crowds saw this they were filled with awe and glorified God who had given such authority to men
verses.literalPt: E a multidão, vendo isto, maravilhou-se, e glorificou a Deus, que dera tal poder aos homens.

verses.original: Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai paragōn ho Iēsous ekeithen eiden anthrōpon kathēmenon epi to telōnion Maththaion legomenon kai legei autō Akolouthei moi kai anastas ēkolouthēsen autō
verses.literal: As Jesus went on from there He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth Follow Me He told him and Matthew got up and followed Him
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, passando adiante dali, viu assentado na recebedoria um homem, chamado Mateus, e disse-lhe: Segue-me. E ele, levantando-se, o seguiu.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto autou anakeimenou en tē oikia kai idou polloi telōnai kai hamartōloi elthontes synanekeinto tō Iēsou kai tois mathētais autou
verses.literal: Later as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house - many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, estando ele em casa sentado à mesa, chegaram muitos publicanos e pecadores, e sentaram-se juntamente com Jesus e seus discípulos.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: kai idontes hoi Pharisaioi elegon tois mathētais autou Dia ti meta tōn telōnōn kai hamartōlōn esthiei ho didaskalos hymōn
verses.literal: When the Pharisees saw this they asked His disciples Why . . . does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners
verses.literalPt: E os fariseus, vendo isto, disseram aos seus discípulos: Por que come o vosso Mestre com os publicanos e pecadores?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας εἶπεν Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλ’ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες
verses.transliteration: Ho de akousas eipen Ou chreian echousin hoi ischyontes iatrou all’ hoi kakōs echontes
verses.literal: On hearing this Jesus said It is not the healthy who need a doctor but the sick
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, ouvindo, disse-lhes: Não necessitam de médico os sãos, mas, sim, os doentes.

verses.original: πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς
verses.transliteration: poreuthentes de mathete ti estin Eleos thelō kai ou thysian ou gar ēlthon kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous
verses.literal: But go and learn what this means I desire mercy not sacrifice For I have not come . . . to call the righteous but sinners
verses.literalPt: Ide, porém, e aprendei o que significa: Misericórdia quero, e não sacrifício. Porque eu não vim a chamar os justos, mas os pecadores, ao arrependimento.

verses.original: Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν πολλά οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν
verses.transliteration: Tote proserchontai autō hoi mathētai Iōannou legontes Dia ti hēmeis kai hoi Pharisaioi nēsteuomen polla hoi de mathētai sou ou nēsteuousin
verses.literal: Then John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked Why is it that . . . we and the Pharisees fast so often but Your disciples do not fast
verses.literalPt: Então, chegaram ao pé dele os discípulos de João, dizendo: Por que jejuamos nós e os fariseus muitas vezes, e os teus discípulos não jejuam?

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφ’ ὅσον μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autois ho Iēsous Mē dynantai hoi huioi tou nymphōnos penthein eph’ hoson met’ autōn estin ho nymphios eleusontai de hēmerai hotan aparthē ap’ autōn ho nymphios kai tote nēsteusousin
verses.literal: Jesus replied How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them then they will fast
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhes Jesus: Podem porventura andar tristes os filhos das bodas, enquanto o esposo está com eles? Dias, porém, virão, em que lhes será tirado o esposo, e então jejuarão.

verses.original: Οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται
verses.transliteration: Oudeis de epiballei epiblēma rhakous agnaphou epi himatiō palaiō airei gar to plērōma autou apo tou himatiou kai cheiron schisma ginetai
verses.literal: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment For the patch will pull away from the garment and a worse tear will result
verses.literalPt: Ninguém deita remendo de pano novo em roupa velha, porque semelhante remendo rompe a roupa, e faz-se maior a rotura.

verses.original: Οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπόλλυνται ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται
verses.transliteration: Oude ballousin oinon neon eis askous palaious ei de mē¦ge rhēgnyntai hoi askoi kai ho oinos ekcheitai kai hoi askoi apollyntai alla ballousin oinon neon eis askous kainous kai amphoteroi syntērountai
verses.literal: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins If they do . . . . . . the skins will burst the wine will spill and the wineskins will be ruined Instead they pour new wine into new wineskins and both are preserved
verses.literalPt: Nem se deita vinho novo em odres velhos; aliás rompem-se os odres, e entorna-se o vinho, e os odres estragam-se; mas deita-se vinho novo em odres novos, e assim ambos se conservam.

verses.original: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπ’ αὐτήν καὶ ζήσεται
verses.transliteration: Tauta autou lalountos autois idou archōn heis elthōn prosekynei autō legōn hoti Hē thygatēr mou arti eteleutēsen alla elthōn epithes tēn cheira sou ep’ autēn kai zēsetai
verses.literal: While Jesus was saying these things a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him My daughter has just died he said But come and place Your hand on her and she will live
verses.literalPt: Dizendo-lhes ele estas coisas, eis que chegou um chefe, e o adorou, dizendo: Minha filha faleceu agora mesmo; mas vem, impõe-lhe a tua mão, e ela viverá.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai egertheis ho Iēsous ēkolouthei autō kai hoi mathētai autou
verses.literal: So Jesus got up and went with him along with His disciples
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, levantando-se, seguiu-o, ele e os seus discípulos.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai idou gynē haimorroousa dōdeka etē proselthousa opisthen hēpsato tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou
verses.literal: Suddenly a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His cloak
verses.literalPt: E eis que uma mulher que havia já doze anos padecia de um fluxo de sangue, chegando por detrás dele, tocou a orla de sua roupa;

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι
verses.transliteration: elegen gar en heautē Ean monon hapsōmai tou himatiou autou sōthēsomai
verses.literal: She said to herself If only I touch His cloak I will be healed
verses.literalPt: Porque dizia consigo: Se eu tão-somente tocar a sua roupa, ficarei sã.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν Θάρσει θύγατερ ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε καὶ ἐσώθη ἡ γυνὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous strapheis kai idōn autēn eipen Tharsei thygater hē pistis sou sesōken se kai esōthē hē gynē apo tēs hōras ekeinēs
verses.literal: Jesus turned and saw her Take courage daughter He said your faith has healed you And the woman was healed from that very hour
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, voltando-se, e vendo-a, disse: Tem ânimo, filha, a tua fé te salvou. E imediatamente a mulher ficou sã.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς αὐλητὰς καὶ τὸν ὄχλον θορυβούμενον
verses.transliteration: Kai elthōn ho Iēsous eis tēn oikian tou archontos kai idōn tous aulētas kai ton ochlon thoryboumenon
verses.literal: When Jesus entered . . . the house of the synagogue leader He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, chegando à casa daquele chefe, e vendo os instrumentistas, e o povo em alvoroço,

verses.original: ἔλεγεν Ἀναχωρεῖτε οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τὸ κοράσιον ἀλλὰ καθεύδει καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: elegen Anachōreite ou gar apethanen to korasion alla katheudei kai kategelōn autou
verses.literal: Go away He told them The girl is not dead . . . but asleep And they laughed at Him
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhes: Retirai-vos, que a menina não está morta, mas dorme. E riam-se dele.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἐξεβλήθη ὁ ὄχλος εἰσελθὼν ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ ἠγέρθη τὸ κοράσιον
verses.transliteration: Hote de exeblēthē ho ochlos eiselthōn ekratēsen tēs cheiros autēs kai ēgerthē to korasion
verses.literal: After . . . the crowd had been put outside Jesus went in and took the girl by the hand and she got up
verses.literalPt: E, logo que o povo foi posto fora, entrou Jesus, e pegou-lhe na mão, e a menina levantou-se.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ φήμη αὕτη εἰς ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἐκείνην
verses.transliteration: kai exēlthen hē phēmē hautē eis holēn tēn gēn ekeinēn
verses.literal: And the news about this spread throughout . . . that region
verses.literalPt: E espalhou-se aquela notícia por todo aquele país.

verses.original: Καὶ παράγοντι ἐκεῖθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ δύο τυφλοὶ κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς υἱὸς Δαυίδ
verses.transliteration: Kai paragonti ekeithen tō Iēsou ēkolouthēsan autō dyo typhloi krazontes kai legontes Eleēson hēmas huios Dauid
verses.literal: As Jesus went on from there two blind men followed Him crying out - Have mercy on us Son of David
verses.literalPt: E, partindo Jesus dali, seguiram-no dois cegos, clamando, e dizendo: Tem compaixão de nós, filho de Davi.

verses.original: Ἐλθόντι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ τυφλοί καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ναί Κύριε
verses.transliteration: Elthonti de eis tēn oikian prosēlthon autō hoi typhloi kai legei autois ho Iēsous Pisteuete hoti dynamai touto poiēsai Legousin autō Nai Kyrie
verses.literal: After Jesus had entered the house the blind men came to Him Do you believe that I am able to do this - He asked Yes Lord they answered
verses.literalPt: E, quando chegou à casa, os cegos se aproximaram dele; e Jesus disse-lhes: Credes vós que eu possa fazer isto? Disseram-lhe eles: Sim, Senhor.

verses.original: Τότε ἥψατο τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν λέγων Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν γενηθήτω ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Tote hēpsato tōn ophthalmōn autōn legōn Kata tēn pistin hymōn genēthētō hymin
verses.literal: Then He touched their eyes and said According to your faith will it be done to you
verses.literalPt: Tocou então os olhos deles, dizendo: Seja-vos feito segundo a vossa fé.

verses.original: καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί καὶ ἐνεβριμήθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Ὁρᾶτε μηδεὶς γινωσκέτω
verses.transliteration: kai ēneōchthēsan autōn hoi ophthalmoi kai enebrimēthē autois ho Iēsous legōn Horate mēdeis ginōsketō
verses.literal: And their eyes were opened - Jesus warned them sternly . . . See that no one finds out about this
verses.literalPt: E os olhos se lhes abriram. E Jesus ameaçou-os, dizendo: Olhai que ninguém o saiba.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες διεφήμισαν αὐτὸν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ
verses.transliteration: hoi de exelthontes diephēmisan auton en holē tē gē ekeinē
verses.literal: But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout . . . . . . the land
verses.literalPt: Mas, tendo eles saído, divulgaram a sua fama por toda aquela terra.

verses.original: Αὐτῶν δὲ ἐξερχομένων ἰδοὺ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπον κωφὸν δαιμονιζόμενον
verses.transliteration: Autōn de exerchomenōn idou prosēnenkan autō anthrōpon kōphon daimonizomenon
verses.literal: As they were leaving a demon-possessed man who was mute was brought to Jesus
verses.literalPt: E, havendo-se eles retirado, trouxeram-lhe um homem mudo e endemoninhado.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκβληθέντος τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες Οὐδέποτε ἐφάνη οὕτως ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ
verses.transliteration: kai ekblēthentos tou daimoniou elalēsen ho kōphos kai ethaumasan hoi ochloi legontes Oudepote ephanē houtōs en tō Israēl
verses.literal: And when the demon had been driven out the man began to speak The crowds were amazed and said Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel
verses.literalPt: E, expulso o demônio, falou o mudo; e a multidão se maravilhou, dizendo: Nunca tal se viu em Israel.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια
verses.transliteration: Hoi de Pharisaioi elegon En tō archonti tōn daimoniōn ekballei ta daimonia
verses.literal: But the Pharisees said It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons
verses.literalPt: Mas os fariseus diziam: Ele expulsa os demônios pelo príncipe dos demônios.

verses.original: Καὶ περιῆγεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς πόλεις πάσας καὶ τὰς κώμας διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν
verses.transliteration: Kai periēgen ho Iēsous tas poleis pasas kai tas kōmas didaskōn en tais synagōgais autōn kai kēryssōn to euangelion tēs basileias kai therapeuōn pasan noson kai pasan malakian
verses.literal: Jesus went through all the towns and villages teaching in their synagogues preaching the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and sickness
verses.literalPt: E percorria Jesus todas as cidades e aldeias, ensinando nas sinagogas deles, e pregando o evangelho do reino, e curando todas as enfermidades e moléstias entre o povo.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἐσπλαγχνίσθη περὶ αὐτῶν ὅτι ἦσαν ἐσκυλμένοι καὶ ἐρριμμένοι ὡσεὶ πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα
verses.transliteration: Idōn de tous ochlous esplanchnisthē peri autōn hoti ēsan eskylmenoi kai errimmenoi hōsei probata mē echonta poimena
verses.literal: When He saw the crowds He was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and helpless like sheep without . . . a shepherd
verses.literalPt: E, vendo as multidões, teve grande compaixão delas, porque andavam cansadas e desgarradas, como ovelhas que não têm pastor.

verses.original: Τότε λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι
verses.transliteration: Tote legei tois mathētais autou Ho men therismos polys hoi de ergatai oligoi
verses.literal: Then He said to His disciples The harvest is plentiful but the workers are few
verses.literalPt: Então, disse aos seus discípulos: A seara é realmente grande, mas poucos os ceifeiros.

verses.original: δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ Κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐκβάλῃ ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: deēthēte oun tou Kyriou tou therismou hopōs ekbalē ergatas eis ton therismon autou
verses.literal: Ask the Lord of the harvest therefore to send out workers into His harvest
verses.literalPt: Rogai, pois, ao Senhor da seara, que mande ceifeiros para a sua seara.
